variables.claim_asserts: Across all 4096 two-state, two-color machines under Wolfram's convention, observed halting-time growth rates are linear, quadratic, or exponential, and exponential computations have bounded-time equivalents.
variables.test_measures: Finite-input maximum halting-time curves T(n), classified by exact or 15%-RMS fits, plus exact partial-function identity including non-halting inputs.

modality.note: Exhaustive machine enumeration under the stated convention is the correct modality and reproduces the book's principal census and example formulas.

assumptions.note: The decisive classifier treats bounded parity or period-4 modulation around linear or quadratic growth as a different growth rate, and the partner criterion requires identical undefined-input patterns rather than the halting-domain equivalence under which all exponential cases have constant-time partners.

scope.claim_scope: All 4096 two-state, two-color Turing machines under Wolfram's halting convention.
scope.test_scope: All 4096 machines, but functions and T(n) are inferred from x <= 1023, with selected machines extended through x <= 16383.

reasons: The enumeration itself is highly aligned: it exactly reproduces 748 never-halting, 3348 sometimes-halting, 1683 always-halting machines and all listed example formulas.

The refutation's 49 'other' pairs are not other growth rates: the supplementary parity-aware analysis classifies them as constant, linear, or quadratic except two quadratic curves with period-4 modulation.

For example, machine 791 has T(n) = 7,19,15,27,23,35,31,43,..., a linear trend with bounded parity modulation; rejecting it for exceeding a 0.15 RMS fit does not test the claimed growth-rate category.

The second failure comes from counting undefined inputs as part of function identity; on each exponential machine's halting domain, the derived results find 261-269 constant-time partners, matching the claim's substantive bounded-computation comparison.
what_would_change_it: Classify growth rates allowing bounded periodic modulation and initial transients, and apply Wolfram's intended equivalence convention for partial functions; retain the exact 4096-machine census and extend inputs only as a robustness check.
